model_interpretation.claim: A simple 32x64x64 blocked schedule with a scalar 4x4 output microkernel should replace the baseline's strided B-column traversal with contiguous four-value loads and expose independent accumulators, while reusing panels through cache blocking. Initializing accumulators on the first reduction block should fully overwrite C without a separate zeroing pass. Keeping packing, explicit ISA intrinsics, and parallelism out of this candidate makes the effect of blocking and the microkernel attributable.

items.subject: Blocked GEMM, packing, and register microkernels
items.objective: Use a blocked GEMM with a register-oriented output microkernel as the primary approach. Measure simple blocking separately from optional packing, explicit SIMD, and parallel tile ownership so gains and regressions can be attributed; include packing and scratch allocation in timed cost. Where useful, compare C initialization by zeroing once against safely overwriting on the first reduction block. Use only compiler/ISA mechanisms supported by the frozen target, respect the caller’s thread budget, and preserve the fixed FP32 tolerance and complete overwrite on every call. Validate all official sizes, compare repeated native n=1024 timings, and record unsuccessful variants.
